Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Victoria 3 building icon, square, with the existing rounded brass frame.
Input images: Image 1 is the exact current cement works icon and EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is supporting insert reference: use ONLY its right-hand cement sack and grey cement powder, not its left limestone blocks.
Primary request: replace the large foreground metal pouring vessel, wheel and stream of molten metal at the lower right of Image 1 with an open burlap sack of grey cement and a small pile of cement powder, matching Image 2's cement. Make cement the clear foreground commodity.
Invariants: preserve the recognizable factory interior behind it, brick furnace, overhead channels, original perspective, warm muted painterly palette and original rounded metallic frame. Do not redesign the building as an outdoor factory. Preserve the composition outside the edited foreground area. Match lighting, grain and scale to the small painted original rather than attaching a photoreal cutout.
Constraints: genuine alpha ONLY outside the rounded frame, opaque scene inside it; no black outer square; no molten metal left in the foreground, no labels, no typography, no watermark. Single finished icon, not a comparison or sheet.

Use case: background-extraction.
Asset type: supplied game building icon cutout.
Input image 1: edit target. Remove ONLY the black pixels outside the existing rounded metallic frame and stray tiny colored specks outside the frame. Output genuine transparent alpha outside that frame.
Invariants: retain the entire frame and its exact shape, quarry landscape, limestone blocks, crane, trees, colors, light and composition, without restyling or replacing anything. Keep all the area inside the frame opaque. This is only an outer-corner background removal, not a new quarry illustration. Square output, no additional border or text.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one square production-method icon for a Victoria 3 mod, legible at 32 pixels.
Input image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its muted amethyst-purple monochrome, chiseled metallic bas-relief, beveled highlights, dark purple crevices and lightly faceted grain. Do not draw the reference crusher.
Composition: single compact centered symbol, entire silhouette visible, generous 10 percent margin, three-quarter view. Genuine transparent alpha around and between components. NO black rectangle, colored background, frame, level numeral, caption, watermark or logos. One finished icon, not a sheet.
Primary subject: a small masonry vertical fixed lime/cement kiln, simple arched firing opening and one rough limestone block. The kiln is the dominant symbol, minimal details, historically plausible before rotary kilns. No factory background, no smoke cloud obscuring silhouette, no water droplet.

Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: one square full-canvas opaque military unit illustration for Victoria 3 mod 1776; recognizable at 80 pixels.
Input image 1 is ONLY a painted style and composition reference sheet: match its restrained oil-painted realism, soft brushwork, muted earth colors, light outdoor haze, strong readable foreground silhouette and secondary soldiers. Do not copy the sheet layout, text, modern shakos or uniforms.
Constraints: one cohesive scene only, no border or labels, no flags or insignia, no watermark, no modern equipment. Historical European visual fallback, not asserted to represent all cultures. Primary subject: three musketeers circa 1700 to 1776. Foreground infantryman in a simple dark blue wool coat, pale waistcoat, weathered black tricorn and crossbelt holds a long flintlock musket vertically while ramming its barrel with the ramrod. His two comrades behind him hold flintlock muskets ready on a grassy field under a pale smoky sky. Show plausible muskets, gripping hands and loading action. The dominant musketeer and long wooden musket are readily recognizable; avoid nineteenth-century tall cylindrical shakos, cartridge magazines and modern rifles.
